name: Content Structuring Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building content structuring — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary content structuring tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building content structuring — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary content structuring tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When content structuring guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to content structuring (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. Prefer explicit, readable content structuring solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
4. State assumptions about content structuring explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen content structuring approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Prefer the simplest content structuring approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
7. Check that content structuring terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
8. Before starting content structuring work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
9. Keep content structuring changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
10. When multiple content structuring strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new content structuring abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting content structuring assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop content structuring edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for content structuring, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
